nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Project Memory (Booking & Appointment System)
nodes.rationale: Single project-memory file with two halves: (A) bootcamp/doc conventions, (B) booking-system domain logic. Read before any work so decisions and gotchas are not re-litigated.

nodes.label: User Entity (single entity + role field)
nodes.rationale: One User entity carrying a role field instead of a separate Provider entity — avoids duplicating identity/auth and lets a provider act as a consumer without a second account.

nodes.label: Role: CONSUMER
nodes.rationale: Browses services and books appointments; the only role with a dedicated /appointments page.

nodes.label: Role: PROVIDER
nodes.rationale: Offers one or more services via UserService N:M and self-manages personal availability including bulk generation. Built from the start, deliberately not deferred to future work.

nodes.label: Role: ADMIN
nodes.rationale: Full permissions: manage services, all users, all appointments, and bulk-generate availability for any provider.

nodes.label: UserService (provider↔service N:M)
nodes.rationale: N:M mapping so a provider can offer multiple services; owning side is User.services, which is what makes the Hibernate inverse-side staleness gotcha reachable.

nodes.label: AvailabilitySlot Entity
nodes.rationale: Belongs to a provider (a User with role PROVIDER), never to a service — the single decision the whole booking model rests on.

nodes.label: Service Entity (com.ammar.bookingsystem.service.Service)
nodes.rationale: Package/class name intentionally matches the domain/ERD rather than being renamed to dodge the Spring @Service annotation clash.

nodes.label: BookingService (booking logic bean)
nodes.rationale: Server-side authority for booking rules: rejects self-booking (400) before the DB, and owns updateStatus role/time/terminal-state gates.

nodes.label: BookingStatus (5 statuses)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED (initial) → CANCELLED / COMPLETED / NO_SHOW terminal states; VACANT exists as a Java enum value but is excluded by the V7 DB CHECK constraint so it can never be persisted.

nodes.label: AppSettings (single-row settings table)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a single-row table, not a generic key/value store: the admin's live booking horizon must survive restarts, apply immediately, and stay cheap to cache in memory.

nodes.label: GoogleAccountConnection Entity
nodes.rationale: Per-provider Google OAuth link with an encrypted refresh token; a provider is not bookable until connected.

nodes.label: Core Rule: Appointments Bound to Provider Availability
nodes.rationale: If slots hung off services, a provider offering 5 services with 5 daily slots would falsely advertise 25 bookable appointments. Binding slots to the provider keeps the real capacity honest.
nodes.norm_label: core rule: appointments bound to provider availability

nodes.label: Rule: Booking One Service Reserves the Slot Across All That Provider's Services
nodes.rationale: Direct consequence of slots belonging to the provider: one human cannot be in two appointments at once, so the reservation must be visible from every service they offer.
nodes.norm_label: rule: booking one service reserves the slot across all that provider's services

nodes.label: Rule: Provider May Book Others, Never Their Own Availability
nodes.rationale: Enforced twice — the day view filters the provider's own entry client-side, and BookingService rejects it with 400 server-side before it reaches the DB. The client filter is explicitly not trusted.
nodes.norm_label: rule: provider may book others, never their own availability

nodes.label: Stacked Provider Dropdowns (day-view slot browsing)
nodes.rationale: Chosen option 2 (provider-preferred times): each provider is a dropdown and several can be open at once so the consumer can compare, and the list scrolls as provider count grows.

nodes.label: Booking Horizon (admin-configurable, default 6 months)
nodes.rationale: Default in application.yaml (booking.max-horizon-months: 6) via @ConfigurationProperties; live admin value in AppSettings. Enforced in two places — calendar UI and server-side booking validation.

nodes.label: Provider Advance Limit (ceil(horizon × multiplier), default 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Providers/admins must pre-load availability further ahead than consumers can book (9 months at horizon 6). Multiplier is yaml-only, not admin-facing; the window rolls so pre-loaded slots become bookable over time.

nodes.label: Calendar Navigation Constrained to the Booking Window
nodes.rationale: Year picker lists only the 1–2 years the window spans; the 12-month grid shadows months before today and beyond the horizon; past days are non-selectable and non-navigable.
nodes.norm_label: calendar navigation constrained to the booking window

nodes.label: Calendar Pressure Coloring (available/total per day)
nodes.rationale: ≥4 available = low pressure (green/lighter), 3 = medium (yellow), 1–2 = about to run out (warm/alert), 0 = shadowed. Colors derived from the site palette so pressure signalling never disrupts the brand.

nodes.label: Rule: Weekends Are Not Special — Shadowing Follows Slot Availability Only
nodes.rationale: A Fri/Sat with provider slots renders by its pressure; a weekday with none is shadowed. A provider may legitimately choose to work weekends, so the calendar must not hardcode a weekend concept.
nodes.norm_label: rule: weekends are not special — shadowing follows slot availability only

nodes.label: All Slots Render; Booked Ones Styled Distinctly
nodes.rationale: Showing booked slots shadowed (rather than hiding them) tells the consumer appointments existed on that date but are taken, which reads as a fuller, more trustworthy schedule.
nodes.norm_label: all slots render; booked ones styled distinctly

nodes.label: Booking Confirmation UX (enabled button + success toast)
nodes.rationale: Button looks disabled until a slot is selected; on success a corner toast auto-dismisses after ~30s with an 'x' to close early, naming service, date, time and confirming the email was sent.
nodes.norm_label: booking confirmation ux (enabled button + success toast)

nodes.label: Booking Status Lifecycle & Gates
nodes.rationale: CANCELLED only >24h before start and frees the slot back to AVAILABLE; COMPLETED only after slot end (provider/admin); NO_SHOW only after end and leaves the slot BOOKED; terminal states are final → 409.

nodes.label: VACANT Is Synthesized, Never Persisted
nodes.rationale: A dashboard-only label for open AVAILABLE slots, emitted with a negative id (=-slotId) and null consumer. The V7 DB CHECK constraint deliberately excludes it so code cannot write it even though it is a Java enum value.

nodes.label: PATCH /api/bookings/{id}/status
nodes.rationale: Single transition entry point into BookingService.updateStatus; the server is the real gate while the modal only shadows disallowed buttons.

nodes.label: Landing Page (public)
nodes.rationale: Hero → How-it-works/journey → Services preview → optional FAQ → Footer (research R3). Deliberately no social-proof section — an MVP has no proof to show.

nodes.label: Booking Page (public service browse)
nodes.rationale: Browsing is open to anonymous users; attempting to book prompts sign-in/sign-up and then redirects back to the exact flow the user was on.

nodes.label: Calendar / Slot Selection Page (/book/[serviceId])
nodes.rationale: A dedicated page rather than a modal (research R4) — supports a multi-step flow, a shareable URL, and a clean auth-redirect back into the flow.

nodes.label: Shared Dashboard (/dashboard — provider + admin)
nodes.rationale: Same UI for both roles (research R2); admins get the extra provider filter. Providers see only their own data plus their own consumer-side bookings.

nodes.label: My Appointments (/appointments — consumer-only)
nodes.rationale: Nav link hidden and direct navigation redirects providers/admins to /dashboard. Backed by GET /api/bookings?mine=true, self-scoped server-side — the client is never trusted for scoping.

nodes.label: "(You)" Merge for Viewer-as-Consumer Rows
nodes.rationale: Providers/admins get no separate 'my bookings' page; their own consumer-side bookings merge into /dashboard with the name bolded and a trailing '(You)' so the row does not read as a real patient.

nodes.label: AppointmentDetailsModal (shared, both tables)
nodes.rationale: Every row in both appointment tables opens it; it is the only place the meeting link is shown, and it shows role-appropriate status buttons while shadowing disallowed ones with an explanatory note.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay (blurred full-page wait)
nodes.rationale: The Book button triggers a synchronous Google Calendar + email round-trip slow enough to feel broken. Content stays visible under the blur (never disappears); the confirmation toast is carried across the redirect via query params, cleared immediately so a refresh doesn't re-show it.

nodes.label: Bulk Availability Generator (weekdays × date range × time ranges)
nodes.rationale: Available to providers for their own slots and to admins for any provider — entering slots one by one would make the system unusable.
nodes.norm_label: bulk availability generator (weekdays × date range × time ranges)

nodes.label: /dashboard/connect-google
nodes.rationale: Shows which Google account is connected — the reason the userinfo.email scope was added beyond the original spec.

nodes.label: Shared Dashboard Filter System
nodes.rationale: Service / Status / Provider (admin-only) multi-selects plus a date-range picker defaulting to today, applied to every section of the page rather than per-widget.

nodes.label: Stat Cards (4, date-range-driven)
nodes.rationale: Narrowed by service+provider but deliberately NOT by the status filter — each card has an intrinsic status meaning (a no-show rate needs completed+no_show regardless of what the user filtered).

nodes.label: "Bookings over time" Chart + Month/Week/Day Toggle
nodes.rationale: Chart and calendar share one granularity toggle anchored at the range start; calendar month is a real 42-cell (6×7) calendar-aligned grid, not a flat day list.

nodes.label: GET /api/bookings/{feed,stats,chart}
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated serviceIds/statuses/providerIds plus from/to. feed returns real bookings plus synthesized VACANT entries, excluded when a specific service is filtered and only when VACANT is among selected statuses.

nodes.label: Confirmation Email via Gmail SMTP
nodes.rationale: Sent to BOTH parties on every booking — consumer confirmation plus a separate provider notification naming the consumer, so the provider learns of a new appointment without checking the dashboard.

nodes.label: Google Meet Links via Google Calendar API
nodes.rationale: events.insert with conferenceDataVersion=1 + conferenceData.createRequest + hangoutsMeet under OAuth2. Feasible on a free Gmail (Workspace only needed for the Admin SDK path); the link comes back as a plain string so the custom UI is preserved.
nodes.norm_label: google meet links via google calendar api

nodes.label: Per-Provider Google OAuth Connection
nodes.rationale: Each provider connects their own account once (scopes calendar.events + userinfo.email; refresh token stored encrypted). The event lands on the provider's calendar with attendees=[consumer, provider] and sendUpdates=all so the provider is host and guests join directly with no manual admit.

nodes.label: Fallback: Provider-Pasted Persistent Meet Link
nodes.rationale: A provider is not bookable until connected, so a manual persistent personal Meet link keeps the system usable when OAuth cannot be completed.

nodes.label: RBAC — Spring Security Filter Chain + Method-Level Authorization
nodes.rationale: Baseline pattern from common_blueprints.md §1. Security review is an explicit step: attempt unauthorized page/action access and confirm it is blocked.
nodes.norm_label: rbac — spring security filter chain + method-level authorization

nodes.label: JWT Bearer Auth (security/ package)
nodes.rationale: JwtService, JwtAuthenticationFilter, AppUserDetailsService, UserPrincipal, CurrentUser. Only /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login are public — never permitAll the whole /api/auth/** because /me must require authentication.

nodes.label: common_blueprints.md §1 (RBAC baseline)
nodes.rationale: External blueprint cited as the RBAC baseline pattern for this project.

nodes.label: Backend: Spring Boot 4.1.0 + Spring Data JPA (JVM 21)
nodes.rationale: Initializr default; docs originally said '3'. ddl-auto: validate — Flyway owns the schema and Hibernate only checks entities match it.
nodes.norm_label: backend: spring boot 4.1.0 + spring data jpa (jvm 21)

nodes.label: Flyway Schema Migrations (db/migration/)
nodes.rationale: Flyway is the schema owner; V7 carries the BookingStatus CHECK constraint that excludes VACANT.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL — Native Windows PG16 Service for Local Dev
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a Docker container after U3 hit a port-5432 conflict with an existing docker-less local Postgres. DB booking_system, user bookingadmin owns the DB so it owns public schema on PG15+ without extra grants. Production still targets managed/containerized Postgres.
nodes.norm_label: postgresql — native windows pg16 service for local dev

nodes.label: spring-dotenv (springboot4-dotenv) for Dev Credentials
nodes.rationale: Loads app/backend/.env (git-ignored) in dev while real env vars still take precedence, so the same config stays safe in production. .env.example is committed with placeholders only.

nodes.label: Frontend: Next.js 16 App Router + React 19 + Tailwind v4
nodes.rationale: create-next-app default (docs originally said '14'), src/ layout in app/frontend. AGENTS.md warns this Next.js has breaking changes vs training data — check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing page code.
nodes.norm_label: frontend: next.js 16 app router + react 19 + tailwind v4

nodes.label: Design System (src/components/ds, via Claude Design + DesignSync)
nodes.rationale: Importable as @/components/ds; ds/screens-reference/ holds visual references only, never imported code.
nodes.norm_label: design system (src/components/ds, via claude design + designsync)

nodes.label: lib/api.ts api() Helper
nodes.rationale: Checks response text before JSON.parse regardless of status code (not just 204), because a 200 with an empty body from a void controller method would otherwise throw on res.json().

nodes.label: UI Libraries: Framer Motion, Embla Carousel, Lucide React
nodes.norm_label: ui libraries: framer motion, embla carousel, lucide react

nodes.label: Gotcha: Flyway Needs spring-boot-starter-flyway on Boot 4
nodes.rationale: FlywayAutoConfiguration moved into its own module — bare flyway-core + flyway-database-postgresql does NOT trigger it and fails SILENTLY: no error, Flyway never runs, DB stays empty. Keep flyway-database-postgresql explicit since it is optional inside the starter.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: flyway needs spring-boot-starter-flyway on boot 4

nodes.label: Convention: @Component, Never @Service
nodes.rationale: Any class importing the Service entity cannot also import org.springframework.stereotype.Service under its simple name. Using @Component everywhere sidesteps the clash uniformly instead of fully-qualifying case by case.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Jackson 3 Relocation (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: Importing com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper compiles fine but throws NoClassDefFoundError at runtime. Spring MVC's own JSON is unaffected; prefer avoiding a direct Jackson dependency in low-level beans like security filters.

nodes.label: Gotcha: SecurityConfig Needs Explicit .exceptionHandling(...)
nodes.rationale: Without an AuthenticationEntryPoint, an unauthenticated/forbidden request surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of 401/403.

nodes.label: Gotcha: @PreAuthorize Denials Need Their Own @ExceptionHandler
nodes.rationale: Method-security AOP throws AccessDeniedException INSIDE the MVC handler invocation, so it never reaches SecurityConfig's filter-level accessDeniedHandler; without a dedicated handler in GlobalExceptionHandler it falls into the blanket Exception catch-all as a 500 instead of 403.

nodes.label: Gotcha: void @DeleteMapping Returns 200 + Empty Body, Not 204
nodes.rationale: Return ResponseEntity.noContent().build() explicitly — an empty-but-200 response breaks naive frontend clients that call res.json() unconditionally on success.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: void @deletemapping returns 200 + empty body, not 204

nodes.label: Gotcha: Hibernate L1 Cache + Inverse-Side @ManyToMany Staleness
nodes.rationale: Mutating the owning side (User.services) then re-fetching the inverse side's owner (Service) in the same persistence context returns the already-loaded instance with a stale lazy collection. Build the response from data you already know is correct instead of re-querying.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: hibernate l1 cache + inverse-side @manytomany staleness

nodes.label: Gotcha: Google OAuth Callback Params Must Be Optional
nodes.rationale: The 'user clicked Cancel' redirect sends error=access_denied with NO code param. Required @RequestParams turn the most common non-happy path into MissingServletRequestParameterException (raw 500). Make them required=false and check for a Google error param before the token exchange.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: google oauth callback params must be optional

nodes.label: Pattern: OAuth state as a Signed, Purpose-Tagged JWT
nodes.rationale: Google's callback is a plain browser redirect with no Authorization header, so the initiating provider's user id travels in a short-lived (10 min) signed token reusing the existing JWT key — the only way a public callback endpoint can know which provider it is for.
nodes.norm_label: pattern: oauth state as a signed, purpose-tagged jwt

nodes.label: Gotcha: spring.mail Nested Properties Need Bracket-Quoted YAML Keys
nodes.rationale: Write "[mail.smtp.ssl.enable]": true, not nested YAML maps. Gmail SMTP on port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS — ssl.enable is what matters, not starttls.enable.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: spring.mail nested properties need bracket-quoted yaml keys

nodes.label: Gotcha: DS Components with Hooks Need "use client"
nodes.rationale: Accordion.jsx used React.useState without "use client" and threw 'useState is not a function' at build time when rendered from a Server Component. Check any newly-pulled DS component for internal hook usage.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: ds components with hooks need "use client"

nodes.label: Gotcha: Public DB-Backed Pages Need force-dynamic
nodes.rationale: Without export const dynamic = "force-dynamic", Next statically bakes the fetch result in at build time and the services preview goes stale.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: public db-backed pages need force-dynamic

nodes.label: Gotcha: Avoid Native number/date/time Inputs (OS-locale rendering)
nodes.rationale: Chromium renders these using the OS locale — on an Arabic machine this produced Arabic-Indic digits and Arabic day/month/hour labels. Use type="text" with YYYY-MM-DD / HH:MM placeholders and regex validation; values stay plain strings either way.

nodes.label: Golden Rules (English §0)
nodes.rationale: Stay inside 3-5 core features · demo data only · plan mode before building · review by using the product not reading its code · context7 for current docs · commit daily · one doc language.

nodes.label: Requirements Standard (English §1)
nodes.rationale: Defers to requirements-standards.md and summarizes EARS patterns, flat FR-/NFR- ids, user stories, Gherkin acceptance criteria, and the Necessary/Atomic/Verifiable/Clear check.

nodes.label: JOURNEY / DECISION text format (English §2)
nodes.rationale: Same structure as the Arabic البنية الموحّدة but with English keywords (JOURNEY/ACTOR/START/DECISION/END); Claude must rewrite the trainee's raw description into it without dropping any step.

nodes.label: The 6-Day Flow (English §3)
nodes.rationale: Day 1 requirements & scope · Day 2 UX plan · Day 3 foundation · Day 4 core function · Day 5 integration & hardening · Day 6 deploy & present — each day ~1h concepts + 1h with trainer + 3h building + 1h review.

nodes.label: Tools Used table (English §5)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code · context7 · draw.io skill · Claude Design · GitHub MCP · chrome-devtools MCP · Vercel — kept as a live table filled in as the bootcamp progresses.

nodes.label: Default Tech Stack & Project Setup (English §6)
nodes.rationale: One full-stack Next.js (TS) app in a single app/ folder — no frontend/backend split — plus hosted Supabase (Postgres + built-in auth, no Docker) and a Vercel deploy; the trainee only creates accounts and pastes keys.

nodes.label: How Claude Works While Building — build, test, report (English §7)
nodes.rationale: Same three testing layers as the Arabic skill (re-runnable automated tests, CLI exercise of server functions, chrome-devtools browser walkthrough), plus the plain-language 'What we'll build now' summary, mandatory password hashing, and explicit server shutdown after testing.
nodes.norm_label: how claude works while building — build, test, report (english §7)

nodes.label: Deploying to Vercel (English §8)
nodes.rationale: Same MCP-plus-CLI split and the same five real-run obstacles as the Arabic deploying skill; the trainee's only manual acts are connecting the MCP and vercel login.

nodes.label: Render Blueprint (render.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure-as-code Blueprint so the backend + managed Postgres can be imported into Render in one step instead of hand-wiring the dashboard.

nodes.label: bookit-db (Render managed Postgres, free plan, oregon)
nodes.rationale: Managed Postgres on the free tier, pinned to the same region as the backend to keep DB latency low.
nodes.norm_label: bookit-db (render managed postgres, free plan, oregon)

nodes.label: bookit-backend (Render docker web service, free plan, oregon)
nodes.rationale: Docker runtime rather than a native Java runtime, so the JVM/Maven build is reproducible from the repo Dockerfile.
nodes.norm_label: bookit-backend (render docker web service, free plan, oregon)

nodes.label: dockerfilePath / dockerContext -> ./app/backend
nodes.rationale: Monorepo: the docker context is scoped to the backend subfolder so the frontend is not shipped into the backend image.

nodes.label: healthCheckPath: /api/services
nodes.rationale: A public, DB-backed GET endpoint is used as the liveness probe, so a green health check also proves the datasource is reachable.

nodes.label: DB_HOST / DB_PORT / DB_NAME / DB_USER / DB_PASSWORD (fromDatabase: bookit-db)
nodes.rationale: Connection values are injected by Render from the linked database rather than typed in, so no DB credential ever lives in the repo. Values are managed by Render and not present in source (redacted).
nodes.norm_label: db_host / db_port / db_name / db_user / db_password (fromdatabase: bookit-db)

nodes.label: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI (pinned https://bookit-backend.onrender.com/api/google/oauth2/callback)
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: the URL is deterministic because the service name is pinned, so the OAuth redirect can be committed rather than filled in after the first deploy.

nodes.label: sync:false secrets (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, JWT_SECRET, EMAIL_USER, EMAIL_PASS)
nodes.rationale: sync:false declares the key without a value so the Blueprint import prompts for it; secret VALUES are deliberately absent from the repo (redacted).
nodes.norm_label: sync:false secrets (google_client_id, google_client_secret, token_encryption_key, jwt_secret, email_user, email_pass)

nodes.label: APP_CORS_ORIGINS (sync:false, set to the Vercel URL post-deploy)
nodes.rationale: Declared as a placeholder so the import prompts for it; the real frontend origin is only known after the Vercel deploy. Value redacted/not in source.
nodes.norm_label: app_cors_origins (sync:false, set to the vercel url post-deploy)

nodes.label: Backend application.yaml
nodes.rationale: Single config surface; every secret is env-var-bound with a dev-safe default so the same file works locally and on Render.

nodes.label: server.port: ${PORT:8080}
nodes.rationale: Comment: Render and most PaaS hosts inject PORT and require the app to bind to it; 8080 is the local fallback where PORT is unset.

nodes.label: spring.datasource url/username/password (DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD)
nodes.rationale: Every part of the JDBC URL is env-overridable with local defaults (localhost:5432/booking_system, user bookingadmin); the password default is empty so a real value must come from the environment. Password value redacted/not in source.
nodes.norm_label: spring.datasource url/username/password (db_host, db_port, db_name, db_user, db_password)

nodes.label: spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto: validate
nodes.rationale: Hibernate is forbidden from mutating the schema; it only checks that entities match what the migrations produced.

nodes.label: spring.flyway.locations: classpath:db/migration + baseline-on-migrate: true
nodes.rationale: Flyway is the sole owner of schema evolution; baseline-on-migrate lets migrations run against a database that already has objects but no Flyway history table.

nodes.label: spring.jpa.show-sql: false
nodes.rationale: SQL logging off by default to keep production logs readable.

nodes.label: spring.mvc.throw-exception-if-no-handler-found: true
nodes.rationale: Makes an unmatched route raise an exception the global handler can turn into a clean JSON 404 instead of Spring's default whitelabel/static fallthrough.

nodes.label: spring.web.resources.add-mappings: false
nodes.rationale: Disables the static-resource handler so unknown paths do not get swallowed by the resource resolver; pairs with throw-exception-if-no-handler-found to make 404s real.

nodes.label: spring.mail host/port (EMAIL_HOST default smtp.gmail.com, EMAIL_PORT default 465)
nodes.rationale: Gmail SMTP on 465 chosen as the confirmation-email transport; both host and port stay env-overridable.
nodes.norm_label: spring.mail host/port (email_host default smtp.gmail.com, email_port default 465)

nodes.label: spring.mail username/password (EMAIL_USER / EMAIL_PASS)
nodes.rationale: Gmail account + app password supplied only via environment; defaults are empty strings. Values redacted/not in source.

nodes.label: [mail.smtp.auth]: true (bracket-quoted YAML key)
nodes.rationale: JavaMail property names contain dots, so they must be written as bracket-quoted single keys rather than nested YAML maps or Spring will not pass them through.

nodes.label: [mail.smtp.ssl.enable]: true (implicit SSL, not STARTTLS)
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS on 587 - this property, not starttls.enable, is what makes JavaMail use SSL for the initial connection.

nodes.label: SMTP timeouts: connectiontimeout / timeout / writetimeout = 10000 ms
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: JavaMail has no default timeout, so a slow/hanging Gmail connection would block the booking thread forever; EmailService's try-catch cannot fire until the socket actually throws.
nodes.norm_label: smtp timeouts: connectiontimeout / timeout / writetimeout = 10000 ms

nodes.label: booking.max-horizon-months: 6 (seed default)
nodes.rationale: Seed value only - the admin's live booking horizon is persisted in the single-row AppSettings table and overrides this at runtime (FR-14/FR-15).

nodes.label: booking.provider-advance-multiplier: 1.5 (not admin-facing)
nodes.rationale: Providers may pre-load availability further ahead than consumers can book; advance limit = ceil(max-horizon-months * multiplier). Deliberately yaml-only so admins cannot change it from the UI.

nodes.label: AppSettings single-row table (runtime override of booking policy)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated single-row table (not a generic key/value store) holds the admin's live horizon so it survives restarts and applies immediately.
nodes.norm_label: appsettings single-row table (runtime override of booking policy)

nodes.label: EmailService (named in the SMTP timeout comment)
nodes.rationale: Referenced by the config comment as the component whose try-catch depends on the socket timeouts to ever fire.
nodes.norm_label: emailservice (named in the smtp timeout comment)

nodes.label: google.client-id / google.client-secret (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)
nodes.rationale: Bound early (M6, FR-6/FR-13) even before the provider-onboarding controller existed; comment notes it is safe to bind now. Values redacted/env-only, defaults empty.

nodes.label: google.redirect-uri (GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, default http://localhost:8080/api/google/oauth2/callback)
nodes.rationale: Local default points at the dev backend so the OAuth loop works without env setup; production value comes from the Render Blueprint.

nodes.label: google.scope: calendar.events + userinfo.email
nodes.rationale: Explicit comment: calendar.events creates/manages the Meet-enabled event; userinfo.email exists purely so the UI can show which Google account is connected.

nodes.label: google.token-encryption-key (TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY)
nodes.rationale: Per-provider Google refresh tokens are stored encrypted at rest, so a separate key is needed beyond the JWT secret. Value redacted/env-only.

nodes.label: app.jwt.secret (JWT_SECRET)
nodes.rationale: Signing key for the M2 JWT bearer auth; env-only with an empty default. Value redacted/not in source.

nodes.label: app.jwt.expiration-ms: 86400000 (24h)
nodes.rationale: 24-hour session length - long enough that a demo run never gets logged out mid-flow.

nodes.label: app.cors.allowed-origins (APP_CORS_ORIGINS, default http://localhost:3000)
nodes.rationale: Split frontend/backend deployment means CORS must be explicitly allowed; the default matches the Next.js dev server so local dev needs no env var.

nodes.label: FR-14 / FR-15 (admin-configurable booking horizon)
nodes.rationale: Requirement IDs cited directly in the config comment, tying the booking keys back to the SRS.

nodes.label: Two-window booking policy (consumer horizon vs provider advance limit)
nodes.rationale: Consumers book within [today, today+horizon] while providers may pre-load availability up to ceil(horizon*multiplier) ahead, so the rolling window always has slots ready to become bookable.

nodes.label: Booking & Appointment Management System (MVP)
nodes.author: AmmarDw
nodes.rationale: Chosen from model #1 of the AI MVP Bootcamp brochure; scope = user registration, service/appointment display, booking management from a dashboard, and confirmation notification.

nodes.label: conversation_history.md Document Protocol
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth surviving context-window limits, session resets and model switches; chat stays a minimal pointer, all prompts/responses live in the file.

nodes.label: PROJECT_REPORT.md (single graded deliverable)
nodes.rationale: One report with TOC: instructions -> template -> generic example -> actual booking-system data, so trainees see both the pattern and a filled example.

nodes.label: research_plan.md (research spikes R1-R4)
nodes.rationale: Registered spikes: R1 Google Meet feasibility, R2 admin dashboard patterns, R3 landing-page sections, R4 calendar UX.

nodes.label: .claude/rules/bootcamp-mvp-process.md
nodes.rationale: Deliberately kept generic so any bootcamp trainee project can use it to guide Claude.

nodes.label: Global i18n + directionality rule
nodes.rationale: Improved, context7-verified rewrite of the legacy i18n_context_system.md blueprint, promoted to a global rule file.

nodes.label: AI_MVP_Bootcamp_6_Days_AR.pdf
nodes.rationale: 6 days / 36h, teams of 2-3, 3-5 core features, demo data only; evaluation weights drive what the docs emphasise.

nodes.label: Lightweight, audience-appropriate documentation stance
nodes.rationale: Target audience is entrepreneurs/students/beginner-intermediate devs, not experts; the capstone report is a style reference only, never a depth target.

nodes.label: User entity (single entity with role field)
nodes.rationale: A separate Provider entity was dropped: one User + a role field (CONSUMER/PROVIDER/ADMIN) covers every case without duplicating identity.
nodes.norm_label: user entity (single entity with role field)

nodes.label: UserService N:M (which services a provider offers)
nodes.rationale: Implemented as a plain @ManyToMany rather than a junction entity, since the join table carries no extra columns.
nodes.norm_label: userservice n:m (which services a provider offers)

nodes.label: Service entity
nodes.rationale: Class name intentionally matches the domain/ERD term even though it collides with Spring's @Service annotation; the project sidesteps this by using @Component for business beans.

nodes.label: GoogleAccountConnection entity
nodes.rationale: Holds userId, googleEmail, encrypted refresh token, scope, connectedAt and a nullable fallbackMeetUrl so a provider is bookable either via OAuth or a pasted persistent link.

nodes.label: AppSettings (single-row typed settings table)
nodes.rationale: application.yaml is read once at startup, packaged in the JAR and often on a read-only filesystem, so it cannot hold a live admin-editable value; a single-row typed table seeded from the yaml default and cached in memory gives one row, one cached read, restart-survival and immediate effect. Live value is cached in memory and refreshed on admin update (AppSettingsCache), so the hot path is one cached read.

nodes.label: Rejected: generic SystemSetting key/value table
nodes.rationale: Over-engineered for a single value; replaced by the typed single-row AppSettings after the user pushed back on adding a whole key/value table for one setting.

nodes.label: Core rule: availability binds to the provider, not the service
nodes.rationale: A provider with 5 daily slots offering 5 services must not appear to have 25 appointments; booking one slot under any service marks it reserved across all that provider's services.
nodes.norm_label: core rule: availability binds to the provider, not the service

nodes.label: uq_provider_slot uniqueness constraint
nodes.rationale: DB-level enforcement of the one-slot-per-provider-per-time rule (FR-4) so overlapping duplicates cannot be created by any code path.

nodes.label: BookingStatus lifecycle (CONFIRMED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED/NO_SHOW/VACANT)
nodes.rationale: Cancel frees the slot back to AVAILABLE, no-show does not (moot anyway, since no-show only applies to past slots that cannot be rebooked); complete/no-show gate on the slot's END time, not its start.

nodes.label: VACANT as a synthesized, never-persisted status
nodes.rationale: A dashboard-only label for open AVAILABLE slots; the V7 CHECK constraint deliberately excludes it so it can never be written even though it is a Java enum value. Added by the V7 migration, whose CHECK constraint deliberately omits VACANT.
nodes.norm_label: vacant as a synthesized, never-persisted status

nodes.label: PATCH /api/bookings/{id}/status role + time gates
nodes.rationale: Enforces role (consumer cancels own >24h out; provider/admin completes after end), time gates, and only-from-CONFIRMED so terminal states are final (409). The UI shadows disallowed buttons but the server is the real gate.

nodes.label: Public landing page
nodes.rationale: Hero -> How-it-works/journey -> Services preview -> FAQ -> Footer; no social-proof section because an MVP has no proof to show.

nodes.label: /book service browsing page (public)
nodes.rationale: Browsing is open; clicking Book when logged out redirects to /sign-in?redirect=/book/{id} so the user returns to exactly where they were. Filtering is a single client-side service-name search box above the grid; no backend query is needed at this scale.

nodes.label: Decision: dedicated booking page, not a modal (R4)
nodes.rationale: The flow is multi-step, the URL should be shareable, and a real route makes the sign-in redirect-back clean.
nodes.norm_label: decision: dedicated booking page, not a modal (r4)

nodes.label: /dashboard shared provider + admin dashboard
nodes.rationale: Same UI for both roles; admin gets extra provider filter/selector. Providers see only their own data, admins see everything. Includes a bookings-over-time chart and a 42-cell (6x7) calendar-aligned month grid sharing one Month/Week/Day granularity toggle, plus role-aware nav.

nodes.label: /appointments 'My Appointments' (consumer-only)
nodes.rationale: Briefly opened to all roles, then reverted to consumer-only: providers/admins already see their own consumer-side bookings merged into /dashboard, so a second page would duplicate data. Direct navigation by a provider/admin redirects to /dashboard.

nodes.label: /dashboard/connect-google provider onboarding screen
nodes.rationale: Three states: not-connected (Connect button + fallback-link paste + not-bookable warning), connected (account email/badge/Disconnect), and a compact dashboard warning banner variant.

nodes.label: Rule: one Claude Design prompt = one screen
nodes.rationale: The combined 'Connect Google + Services mgmt' prompt confused Claude Design about whether to produce one or two artefacts; splitting into single-screen prompts fixed it.
nodes.norm_label: rule: one claude design prompt = one screen

nodes.label: Stacked provider dropdowns for slot selection
nodes.rationale: Chosen over unified admin-defined slots and over a flat time-ordered stack: each provider is a dropdown, several can be open at once to compare, and the list scrolls gracefully as providers grow.
nodes.norm_label: stacked provider dropdowns for slot selection

nodes.label: Calendar pressure colouring (high/medium/low/none)
nodes.rationale: Thresholds: >=4 available = low pressure (green), 3 = medium (amber), 1-2 = about to run out; colours derive from the site palette so they do not disrupt it, reinforced by the number badge and opacity for colourblind safety.

nodes.label: CalendarDayCell design-system component
nodes.rationale: Extended with an optional backward-compatible `total` prop, and later a `full` state so fully-booked days keep their 0/N badge and stay clickable instead of looking empty. Renders the available/total count badge (e.g. 3/8) that FR-9 requires.

nodes.label: Booking success toast (exact text pattern)
nodes.rationale: Auto-dismisses after ~30s with an x to close early. After the redirect change it is carried across via query params which are cleared immediately (router.replace) so a refresh does not re-show it.

nodes.label: LoadingOverlay (blurred full-page wait)
nodes.rationale: The Book button triggers a synchronous Google Calendar + email round-trip that is slow enough to feel broken; the page blurs but never disappears so the user keeps context.

nodes.label: '(You)' marker on merged consumer-side rows
nodes.rationale: Only meaningful where the consumer field varies row-to-row, which /appointments can never be; so provider/admin self-bookings merge into /dashboard and render bold + primary-teal with a trailing (You) so they do not read as a real patient.

nodes.label: Provider cannot book their own availability
nodes.rationale: Enforced twice: the signed-in provider's own entry is filtered out of the day-view list client-side, and BookingService rejects it with 400 before any DB write because the client-side filter is not trusted.
nodes.norm_label: provider cannot book their own availability

nodes.label: Shared AppointmentDetailsModal
nodes.rationale: One details view wired into both the consumer /appointments table and the provider/admin dashboard table, rather than two near-duplicate modals; it is the only place the meeting link is surfaced.

nodes.label: Admin-configurable max booking horizon (default 6 months)
nodes.rationale: Bounds how far ahead consumers can book and keeps the year picker down to 1-2 years and the month grid meaningfully shadowed; enforced in both the calendar UI and server-side booking validation.

nodes.label: Provider advance limit = ceil(horizon x 1.5)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over doubling: +50% (6 -> 9 months) lets providers pre-load availability ahead of the consumer window without a second admin-facing setting; yaml-only multiplier derived from the admin horizon, and the rolling window makes pre-loaded slots bookable as time advances.

nodes.label: Decision: weekends are not special
nodes.rationale: Hard Fri/Sat skipping was removed because providers already pick weekdays explicitly and some may deliberately work weekends as a part-time job; calendar shadowing is now driven purely by having 0 available slots.

nodes.label: Bulk availability generator (weekdays x date range x time ranges)
nodes.rationale: Available to providers (own slots) and admins (any provider); idempotent re-runs skip existing slots and are bounded by the advance limit.
nodes.norm_label: bulk availability generator (weekdays x date range x time ranges)

nodes.label: Decision: bulk generation is non-destructive
nodes.rationale: A deliberate deviation from the Claude Design copy that said 'conflicts will be replaced' — overwriting would risk deleting already-booked slots.

nodes.label: Decision: provider onboarding is admin-managed (FR-16)
nodes.rationale: Public sign-up always yields CONSUMER; only an admin creates providers or promotes a consumer. Consistent with the admin-controlled services model and gives better vetting; a crafted sign-up requesting PROVIDER is a privilege-escalation attempt and still yields CONSUMER.

nodes.label: Decision: no provider filter on the services grid
nodes.rationale: The journey is service-first: providers only become a filtering concept after a service and date are chosen, and provider-first browsing is unscoped new work, not in FR-1.
nodes.norm_label: decision: no provider filter on the services grid

nodes.label: Monorepo layout (app/backend + app/frontend)
nodes.rationale: One Git repository holding both halves rather than two repos; the nested .git created by create-next-app was removed to keep it single-repo.

nodes.label: GitHub repo AmmarDw/booking-system
nodes.author: AmmarDw
nodes.rationale: Created private, with no README/.gitignore/license init so it would not conflict with the Spring-Initializr-generated files already present locally.

nodes.label: R1 — Google Meet link generation feasibility
nodes.rationale: Feasible on a free Gmail via Google Calendar API + OAuth2 (conferenceData.createRequest, hangoutsMeet); the 'Workspace only' claim applies to the Admin-SDK path, not user OAuth. Custom UI is preserved because the link comes back as a plain string.
nodes.norm_label: r1 — google meet link generation feasibility

nodes.label: R4 — Calendar UX (popup vs dedicated page)
nodes.norm_label: r4 — calendar ux (popup vs dedicated page)

nodes.label: Decision: per-provider Google connection from the start
nodes.rationale: Google marks anyone on the event guest list as Trusted so a single host account would not strictly force manual admits — but that model puts every meeting on an absent operator's calendar and any edge case (different email, waiting room on) could only be cleared by them. Per-provider gives correct ownership and better UX. The userinfo.email scope was added beyond the original spec so the connect screen can show which Google account is connected.
nodes.norm_label: decision: per-provider google connection from the start

nodes.label: Fallback: provider pastes a persistent personal Meet link
nodes.rationale: A provider is not bookable until they either connect Google or set a fallback link; the fallback keeps the booking flow usable without OAuth.
nodes.norm_label: fallback: provider pastes a persistent personal meet link

nodes.label: Spring Boot 4.1.0 backend
nodes.rationale: Docs originally said 'Spring Boot 3'; the Initializr default turned out to be 4.1.0 with 4.x starter names, and the docs were reconciled to reality rather than the plan.

nodes.label: Stateless JWT Bearer authentication
nodes.rationale: Chosen with the user over session auth; security/ package holds JwtService, JwtAuthenticationFilter, AppUserDetailsService, UserPrincipal and CurrentUser. Sits on a stateless Spring Security chain with BCrypt and method security enabled.

nodes.label: SecurityConfig filter chain
nodes.rationale: Needs explicit .exceptionHandling(...) entry points — without them an unauthenticated request has no AuthenticationEntryPoint and surfaces as an opaque 500 instead of 401/403.

nodes.label: Bug: /api/auth/** permitAll leaked /me
nodes.rationale: The wildcard matcher also permitted /api/auth/me, so an anonymous request reached the controller and threw IllegalStateException from CurrentUser.get() instead of a clean 401. Fixed by naming /register and /login explicitly.

nodes.label: GlobalExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice)
nodes.rationale: A bare @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) with no logging silently converted real bugs into opaque 500s; logging was added so that class of bug cannot hide again.

nodes.label: Gotcha: @PreAuthorize denials need their own handler
nodes.rationale: Method-security throws AccessDeniedException inside the MVC handler invocation, so it never reaches SecurityConfig's filter-level accessDeniedHandler; without a dedicated @ExceptionHandler it falls into the catch-all as a 500 instead of 403.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: @preauthorize denials need their own handler

nodes.label: Gotcha: void @DeleteMapping returns 200 + empty body
nodes.rationale: The frontend api() helper only special-cased 204 before calling res.json(), so a successful delete surfaced as a UI error. Fixed on both ends: deletes return ResponseEntity.noContent(), and api() checks response text before parsing regardless of status.

nodes.label: Gotcha: stale inverse-side @ManyToMany in the first-level cache
nodes.rationale: After updating the owning side (User.services) and re-fetching Service in the same persistence context, Hibernate returned the already-loaded instance with a stale providers collection. Fixed by building the response from the known-new set instead of re-querying.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: stale inverse-side @manytomany in the first-level cache

nodes.label: Gotcha: Jackson 3 relocation (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper compiles but throws NoClassDefFoundError at runtime on this stack. Framework-managed JSON is unaffected; fixed by hand-writing the small fixed-shape JSON in the security layer rather than depending on Jackson there at all.

nodes.label: Convention: @Component, never @Service
nodes.rationale: Any class importing the Service entity cannot also import org.springframework.stereotype.Service under its simple name; using @Component everywhere sidesteps the clash uniformly instead of fully-qualifying case by case.

nodes.label: Flyway schema migrations
nodes.rationale: Flyway owns the schema; ddl-auto switched from update to validate so Hibernate only checks that entities match the migrated schema.

nodes.label: Gotcha: Spring Boot 4 moved FlywayAutoConfiguration into its own module
nodes.rationale: A bare flyway-core + flyway-database-postgresql never triggers autoconfiguration — it fails silently, so Flyway had never actually run and the earlier 'migrations applied' claim was unverifiable (no entities existed yet, so validate had nothing to check). Fixed with spring-boot-starter-flyway, keeping flyway-database-postgresql explicit since it is optional inside the starter.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: spring boot 4 moved flywayautoconfiguration into its own module

nodes.label: Demo seed migrations (V2-V6)
nodes.rationale: Demo data only per the bootcamp rule. Bcrypt hashes were extracted from real registrations through the app's own /api/auth/register so they are guaranteed encoder-compatible, rather than hand-computed; a demo admin was seeded as a bootstrapping requirement since only an admin can create users.

nodes.label: Native Windows PostgreSQL 16 service (dev)
nodes.rationale: Docker was planned, but port 5432 was already occupied by an existing native service, so the native install was used instead. DB booking_system is owned by bookingadmin — ownership alone grants public-schema rights on PG15+, so no extra GRANTs are needed.

nodes.label: spring-dotenv (springboot4-dotenv) for local secrets
nodes.rationale: Auto-loads .env as a Spring property source in dev while real environment variables still take precedence, so it stays safe in production and needs no manual shell exports locally.

nodes.label: Rule: real values in .env, placeholders only in .env.example
nodes.rationale: The real DB password had been put in .env.example, which is committed by design; only .env is git-ignored. Caught before the project was even a git repo, so no history needed scrubbing.
nodes.norm_label: rule: real values in .env, placeholders only in .env.example

nodes.label: Gotcha: spring-dotenv loads .env from the process working directory
nodes.rationale: ./mvnw runs from app/backend so it worked, but IntelliJ ran from a different directory, leaving DB_PASSWORD empty -> SCRAM auth failure -> 'Unable to determine Dialect' as a downstream symptom. Fix: set the run config working directory to app/backend.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: spring-dotenv loads .env from the process working directory

nodes.label: BookingService (createBooking)
nodes.rationale: @Transactional; validates slot AVAILABLE, within the booking window, that the provider actually offers the requested service, and that the provider is not booking themselves — then flips the slot to BOOKED. Meeting-link and email failures can never fail the booking itself (NFR-4).

nodes.label: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE slot row lock
nodes.rationale: findByIdForUpdate row-locks the slot so two concurrent bookings cannot both see it as AVAILABLE.
nodes.norm_label: select ... for update slot row lock

nodes.label: Availability month/day endpoints
nodes.rationale: month returns per-day available/total counts; day returns providers grouped with their slots, including only providers with at least one slot that day.

nodes.label: GET /api/settings/booking-window (public)
nodes.rationale: Exposes maxHorizonMonths/today/maxBookableDate (later advanceLimitMonths/maxAdvanceDate) so the frontend can bound calendar navigation without trusting the client clock.

nodes.label: AppointmentQueryService (role-scoped listing)
nodes.rationale: Consumers are hard-scoped server-side to their own consumerUserId so filter params like providerId cannot be used to escape the scope; providers see their provider-scoped rows unioned with bookings they made as a consumer elsewhere. Exposed to the frontend as GET /api/bookings?mine=true, which always returns just the caller's own consumer-side bookings regardless of role.

nodes.label: GET /api/bookings/{feed,stats,chart}
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated multi-value serviceIds/statuses/providerIds plus from/to date range; feed adds synthesized VACANT entries with a negative id and null consumer.

nodes.label: Four date-range-driven stat cards
nodes.rationale: The date range fully replaces the fixed today/this-week/30d windows and the labels adapt. Cards are narrowed by service+provider but deliberately not by the status filter, since each card has an intrinsic status meaning (a no-show rate needs completed+no_show regardless).

nodes.label: Shared dashboard filter system
nodes.rationale: Service / Status / Provider (admin-only) multi-selects plus a date range, applied uniformly to every section so no view can silently show a different slice.

nodes.label: EmailService (Gmail SMTP confirmations)
nodes.rationale: Never throws, per NFR-4. Sends two mails per booking: the consumer confirmation (naming provider name+email) and a separate provider notification (naming consumer name+email) so the provider knows without checking the dashboard. Gmail SMTP on port 465 is implicit SSL, not STARTTLS, and the nested spring.mail properties must be written as bracket-quoted YAML keys.

nodes.label: GoogleCalendarService#createMeetingEvent
nodes.rationale: events.insert with conferenceDataVersion=1, hangoutsMeet createRequest, attendees=[consumer, provider] and sendUpdates=all, on the provider's own calendar so they are the organiser who actually attends. Returns null on any failure rather than throwing.

nodes.label: GoogleOAuthService / GoogleOAuthController
nodes.rationale: authorize builds the consent URL with prompt=consent so a refresh token is issued even on reconnect; the callback is public because Google redirects the browser there with no Authorization header.

nodes.label: OAuth state as a short-lived signed JWT
nodes.rationale: Google's callback is a plain browser redirect with no Authorization header, so the JWT filter cannot tell which provider initiated it; a 10-minute purpose-tagged token carrying the provider's user id, signed with the existing key, is the only way to identify them.
nodes.norm_label: oauth state as a short-lived signed jwt

nodes.label: Gotcha: OAuth callback params must be optional
nodes.rationale: A provider clicking Cancel on the consent screen redirects back with error=access_denied and no code param at all; required @RequestParams turned the single most common non-happy path into a raw 500. Caught by deliberately curling that exact shape, not by review.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: oauth callback params must be optional

nodes.label: TokenCipher (AES-256-GCM refresh-token encryption)
nodes.rationale: Key derived via SHA-256 of TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY so any non-empty configured string yields a valid 256-bit key.

nodes.label: Google Cloud project + OAuth client setup (U4)
nodes.rationale: The console is console.cloud.google.com — guessed Google subdomains are a phishing pattern. The 'External' tab no longer exists in the new Google Auth Platform UI (it is the Audience setting from the Get Started wizard), and the redirect URI is a text value pasted into Google's form, not a page to visit.
nodes.norm_label: google cloud project + oauth client setup (u4)

nodes.label: Next.js 16 App Router frontend
nodes.rationale: create-next-app default installed 16 / React 19 / Tailwind v4, reconciling the docs that had said 14 — the same reality-over-plan correction made for Spring Boot. AGENTS.md warns it differs from training data; check node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing page code.

nodes.label: BookIt design system (src/components/ds)
nodes.rationale: Tokens (availability-pressure colours, teal, light/dark, Arabic RTL typography swap) plus 11 ES-module components with a barrel export; the 4 Claude Design screens are kept as visual reference only because they rely on sandbox globals rather than ES imports. Primary token is teal #0D9488, with availability greens/ambers tuned distinct and reinforced by the number badge and opacity for colourblind safety.

nodes.label: Claude Design (design generation tool)
nodes.rationale: Design-System-first, then a separate generation per screen selecting that system — never in the system's own chat and never reusing one screen's chat, so iteration history from one screen cannot bleed into another.

nodes.label: DesignSync (Claude Design -> repo bridge)
nodes.rationale: The /design-sync skill is user-triggered only and cannot be model-invoked, so components were pulled via the DesignSync tool's get_file plus local writes.

nodes.label: Gotcha: DS component hooks without "use client"
nodes.rationale: Accordion.jsx calls React.useState internally but shipped without the directive, so rendering it from the Server Component landing page threw 'useState is not a function' at build time. Fixed at the component, not worked around at the page.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: ds component hooks without "use client"

nodes.label: Gotcha: public DB-backed pages need force-dynamic
nodes.rationale: The landing page built as a static route, baking in whatever the backend returned at build time; export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' makes the services preview live.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: public db-backed pages need force-dynamic

nodes.label: Gotcha: toLocaleDateString(undefined) uses the OS locale
nodes.rationale: Rendered Arabic month names on a machine with an Arabic OS locale even though no i18n was wired up; always pass an explicit 'en-US' until real i18n exists.
nodes.norm_label: gotcha: tolocaledatestring(undefined) uses the os locale

nodes.label: Gotcha: avoid native number/date/time inputs
nodes.rationale: Chromium renders them with the OS locale, producing Arabic-Indic digits and Arabic day/month labels; replaced with type=text plus format placeholders and regex validation. Kept deliberately even where the Claude Design source used native pickers.

nodes.label: src/lib/api.ts fetch wrapper
nodes.rationale: Injects the Bearer token and checks response text before JSON.parse regardless of status, so a 200-with-empty-body cannot throw.

nodes.label: src/lib/auth.tsx (AuthProvider / useAuth)
nodes.rationale: Token store with localStorage persistence; later threaded the user's id through so the UI can answer 'is this row's consumer me' and 'is this provider me'.

nodes.label: Redirect-back after sign-in (?redirect=)
nodes.rationale: FR-2: an unauthenticated user who tries to book is sent to sign-in and returned to exactly the booking flow they were on.

nodes.label: M6.1 — Provider email, My Appointments, details modal
nodes.norm_label: m6.1 — provider email, my appointments, details modal

nodes.label: M6.2 — Redirect, richer emails, overlay, self-booking guard
nodes.norm_label: m6.2 — redirect, richer emails, overlay, self-booking guard
